Operating format

A working room for leaders turning AI into the operating layer.

The session focuses on what happens after tool adoption: where AI touches systems of record, human handoffs, controls, decisions, and measurable workflow output.

Stage 01

Workflow Reality Briefing

A concise opening view of the gap between individual AI productivity and integrated operating capability.

Stage 02

Implementation Constraint Exchange

Moderated prompts surface data readiness, integration debt, ownership, agent boundaries, vendor fit, and adoption friction.

Stage 03

Operating Pattern Handoff

Qualified participants identify workflow patterns that deserve deeper summit work, partner input, and executive research.

The room

Where AI stops being a side tool and starts changing work.

The discussion centers on the real operating questions: what systems AI needs to touch, which workflows should change, where people stay accountable, and how leaders keep work observable.

Audience
CIOs, COOs, CTOs, transformation leaders, product leaders, data leaders, and operators accountable for workflow modernization.
Access
Invitation-only, capped at nine executive participants for a moderated exchange rather than broadcast attendance.
Outcome
A clearer view of the integration decisions required before AI can become reliable operating infrastructure.
Moderated questions

The workflow questions that decide whether AI becomes operational.

Each question is designed to move the conversation from tools and pilots into systems, process, accountability, and daily execution.

01

Which workflows are ready for AI integration?

Where are the process, data, controls, and ownership mature enough for AI to become part of the actual operating flow?

02

What should stay outside the AI workflow?

Which decisions, handoffs, approvals, or customer interactions should remain human-led or explicitly constrained?

03

How much integration debt blocks progress?

Where do fragmented systems, weak APIs, messy data, or unclear process ownership make AI adoption look easier than it is?

04

Who designs the new way of working?

Should workflow redesign be owned by IT, operations, product, business units, transformation teams, or a dedicated AI operating function?

05

Where do agents belong in the workflow?

Which agentic tasks are reliable enough today, and where do leaders need routing, evaluation, escalation, or human approval?

06

How do we observe AI-enabled work?

What logs, metrics, reviews, exception paths, and audit trails are needed when AI participates in operational decisions?

07

How does AI change the employee experience?

Where does workflow AI remove friction, where does it create confusion, and how should leaders redesign roles around it?

08

Which vendors become operating partners?

How should leaders evaluate platforms, orchestration tools, embedded AI products, and implementation partners for workflow-critical work?

Run of show

A direct path from integration constraints to operating patterns.

The session compresses workflow framing, peer comparison, and next-step qualification into one focused executive hour.
